elicitation_input.question: The Scottish-American industrialist and philanthropist Andrew Carnegie (1835-1919) pioneered and made his vast fortune in which industry in late 1800s USA?

llm_generation.text:
Andrew Carnegie made his vast fortune in the **steel industry**.

Through his company, the Carnegie Steel Company, he became the dominant force in American steel production during the late 19th century. Carnegie pioneered the use of the Bessemer process for mass-producing steel efficiently and at lower cost, which was crucial for American industrial expansion—supplying steel for railroads, bridges, and buildings during the era of rapid industrialization.

In 1901, he sold Carnegie Steel to J.P. Morgan, who merged it with other companies to form U.S. Steel, the first billion-dollar corporation in the world. This sale made Carnegie one of the wealthiest people in history at the time.

He subsequently devoted much of his fortune to philanthropy, famously funding public libraries across the United States and other English-speaking countries, as well as supporting education and various charitable causes—reflecting his belief, articulated in his essay "The Gospel of Wealth," that the rich had a moral obligation to give back to society.
